solutions.latex: $$\begin{aligned}y&=\ln x\\ y&=3\ln x\quad\text{(vertical dilation of 3)}\\ y&=3\ln(x+4)\quad\text{(horizontal translation to left 4 units)}\end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned}T_n&=a+(n-1)d\\ T_7=45:\ a+6d&=45\quad\text{(1)}\\ T_{11}=77:\ a+10d&=77\quad\text{(2)}\\ \text{(2)}-\text{(1)}:\ 4d&=32\\ d&=8\quad\text{(3)}\end{aligned}$$
Sub (3) into (1): $45=a+6\times 8$, so $a=-3$.

$a=-3$ and $d=8$

OR axis of symmetry $x=-\dfrac{b}{2a}$:
$$\begin{aligned}y&=-k(x+b)^2+c\\ &=-k(x^2+2xb+b^2)+c\\ &=-kx^2-2kbx-kb^2+c\end{aligned}$$
$$x=-\dfrac{-2kb}{-2k}=-b$$

Area under the curve must equal 1.
$$A=\int_0^5\dfrac{3x^2}{125}\,dx=\dfrac{3}{125}\int_0^5x^2\,dx=\dfrac{3}{125}\left[\dfrac{x^3}{3}\right]_0^5=\dfrac{3}{125}\times\dfrac{125}{3}-0=1$$

solutions.latex:
$$\begin{aligned}\sqrt{x+1}&=11-x\quad\text{squaring both sides}\\ x+1&=(11-x)^2\\ x+1&=121-22x+x^2\\ x^2-23x+120&=0\\ x^2-8x-15x+120&=0\\ (x-8)(x-15)&=0\\ x&=8\text{ or }15\end{aligned}$$
When $x=8$, $y=3$. When $x=15$, $y=-4$.

Other methods of solution are possible.

Since the radical sign implies positive square root, $y=\sqrt{x+1}$ only exists above the $x$ axis, so the point $(15,-4)$ is not part of the solution. The only point of intersection is $(8,3)$.

Gradient of the tangent at $P(2,4)$: $m=\dfrac{dy}{dx}=2^3+2\times 2-7=5$

Equation of the normal: $y-y_1=m(x-x_1)$, $y-4=-\dfrac{1}{5}(x-2)$

$$\therefore\ x+5y-22=0$$
